condition: Product held under vacuum or inert gas is NOT sold or served unless a HACCP plan for reduced-oxygen packaging has been submitted to and accepted by the regulatory authority, and a variance obtained where the chosen control path is not one of the 3-502.12 without-variance routes.
control: HACCP plan; variance application; regulatory authority sign-off

condition: Espresso at pH 5.0-5.4 and aw ~0.99 has no intrinsic barrier. Refrigeration alone at <=5 degC is a single barrier; without a second barrier the without-variance route under 3-502.12(B) is unavailable.
verdict: NO-GO for the "store it for later" concept as drawn
control: Acidify below pH 4.6, OR freeze, OR restrict to <=48 h at <=4 degC under an accepted HACCP plan, OR abandon ROP

condition: If ROP is retained with refrigeration as sole control, product is held at <=3.3 degC (target 1-3 degC) with continuous logging and a time/temperature indicator on each package.
control: Data-logging refrigerator, TTI per package, discard-on-alarm SOP

condition: Chill from 78 degC to <=5 degC is completed inside the Food Code cooling window and documented; the flash-chill plate itself must be validated as achieving it, not assumed.
control: Thermocouple validation runs; CCP with recorded exit temperature per batch

condition: No open LN2 bath in a customer-facing or staff-occupied zone without a fixed oxygen-depletion monitor with a two-stage alarm (warn 20.0 %, evacuate 19.5 %) and a documented ventilation rate.
control: O2 sensors at 0.3 m and 1.5 m AFF within 2 m of the bath; audible/visual alarm inside and outside the zone

condition: Behind-bar zone maintains >=2 nominal air changes per hour of outdoor air with the bath running at up to 10 L/h.
control: Dedicated make-up air, interlocked to the LN2 supply

condition: No footwell, drain pit, floor cooler well, cellar hatch or basement stair within the zone where cold nitrogen can pool. Where one exists, low-level extract at >=20 nominal ACH of the pooled volume, or the device is not sited there.
verdict: NO-GO in any cafe with a below-floor void near the bar
control: Low-level (150 mm AFF) continuous extract; O2 sensor in the void; physical barrier

condition: Bulk LN2 dewar stored outside the occupied zone, in a ventilated enclosure, with the transfer route not passing over a floor void.
control: External dewar cabinet; restricted decanting area; no lone working during decant

condition: No organic material - coffee grounds, milk, paper filters, sugar, cloths, oils - contacts a surface below about 90 K where liquid oxygen can condense.
verdict: NO-GO for an open sloped plate below 90 K in an espresso bar
control: Thermal break so the food-contact surface never falls below ~253 K; or full inert-gas shroud over the cold zone

condition: Any LN2 bath left open to room air is drained and warmed to ambient before end of service; oxygen-enriched residue is never poured onto a floor drain, cloth or refuse.
control: Written warm-up and disposal procedure; no LN2 left standing overnight

condition: No untrained staff member operates or cleans the device. PPE (cryogenic gloves, full face shield, closed non-absorbent footwear, apron without cuffs or pockets) worn for every fill, drain and clean.
control: Documented cryogen training, refreshers, PPE audit; device lockout when trained operator absent

condition: No closed volume anywhere in the LN2 circuit. Every section that can trap liquid has a relief device sized for full boil-off; no ball valves that can isolate liquid between two closed points.
verdict: NO-GO if any trapped volume exists
control: Relief valves / burst discs; open-vent design; annual verification

condition: All materials within the cold zone are rated for 77 K service. Carbon steel, most polymers, standard elastomer gaskets and ordinary glassware are excluded.
control: Austenitic stainless / 6061 Al / C101 Cu in cold zone; PTFE or PCTFE seals; no mild steel fasteners

condition: Food-contact surface is cleaned and sanitised at least every 4 hours during continuous use per Food Code 4-602.11 - which requires warming the plate to ambient, cleaning, sanitising, drying, and re-cooling.
verdict: NO-GO for a continuously cold open plate
control: Duty-cycle the plate: warm/clean/sanitise/re-cool at 4 h intervals, budget the LN2 and downtime; or enclose the flow path

condition: Open food-contact surface is protected from overhead and airborne contamination per Food Code 3-306.11; a frosted plate that continuously condenses ambient air is the opposite of protected.
verdict: NO-GO for an open sloped plate
control: Enclose the chill path (tube-in-block or plate-in-cabinet) with a cleanable, drainable, sanitisable flow channel

condition: An open shared surface downstream of milk, syrups and nut products is a cross-contact route. Allergen-free claims cannot be supported without a dedicated flow path or a full clean between allergen and non-allergen shots.
verdict: GO only with dedicated path or documented changeover
control: Dedicated chill path per allergen class, or wash-down between; allergen matrix in the food safety plan

condition: Food-contact material must be acceptable under Food Code 4-101.11 / NSF-ANSI 51. Bare 6061 aluminium and bare C101 copper in prolonged contact with pH ~5 beverage are corrosion and metal-migration concerns; copper in particular is restricted for acidic foods.
verdict: NO-GO for bare copper food contact
control: Stainless 304/316 food-contact liner or cladding over the conductive core; documented NSF-51 acceptance
